:::{#thm-symmetric-eigenvectors-orthogonal}
#### Eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix for distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal

Let $\matr{A}$ be a symmetric $p \times p$ matrix (@def-symmetric-matrix),
and let $\vecf{u}$ and $\vecf{v}$ be eigenvectors of $\matr{A}$ (@def-eigenvector)
for eigenvalues $\eigval_1 \ne \eigval_2$.
Then $\vecf{u} \perp \vecf{v}$ (@def-orthogonal-vectors).

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\eigval_1\,(\vecf{u} \cdot \vecf{v})
&= (\eigval_1 \vecf{u}) \cdot \vecf{v}
&& \text{(@def-dot-product)}
\\
&= (\matr{A} \vecf{u}) \cdot \vecf{v}
&& \text{(} \vecf{u} \text{ is an eigenvector for } \eigval_1 \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{A} \vecf{u})}\,\vecf{v}
&& \text{(@def-dot-product)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}}\,\tp{\matr{A}}\,\vecf{v}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}}\,\matr{A}\,\vecf{v}
&& \text{(} \matr{A} \text{ is symmetric)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}}\,(\eigval_2 \vecf{v})
&& \text{(} \vecf{v} \text{ is an eigenvector for } \eigval_2 \text{)}
\\
&= \eigval_2\,(\vecf{u} \cdot \vecf{v}).
&& \text{(@def-dot-product)}
\ea
$$

So $(\eigval_1 - \eigval_2)\,(\vecf{u} \cdot \vecf{v}) = 0$,
and $\eigval_1 - \eigval_2 \ne 0$, so $\vecf{u} \cdot \vecf{v} = 0$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-symmetric-eigenvectors-orthogonal}
#### Eigenvectors of a symmetric $2 \times 2$ matrix

$\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ is symmetric.
Its eigenvectors $(1, 1)$ for $\eigval_1 = 3$ and $(1, -1)$ for $\eigval_2 = 1$ (@exm-eigenvalue) satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
(1, 1) \cdot (1, -1) &= 1 \cd 1 + 1 \cd (-1) \\
&= 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
